issues.t: Transmission stops working or loses gears
issues.sym: The SUV hesitates, shifts hard or slips, may get stuck in one gear, and in bad cases stops moving forward or in reverse, often around 75,000 to 85,000 miles.
issues.why: The 6-speed automatic used in these years wears internally (clutches, valve body and solenoids). CarComplaints rates the 2014 as the worst Escape year, mostly for transmission failures.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition and get the codes read at the first sign of slipping. Ask a Ford dealer about software updates, open bulletins or goodwill help before paying for a replacement transmission.

issues.t: 6-speed automatic shifts harshly, slips or fails
issues.sym: Jerky or hard shifts (especially into 2nd and 3rd), slipping when merging or climbing, the engine revving high before a shift, or sudden loss of drive with a warning light.
issues.why: Owners and dealers point to the transmission software, valve body, solenoids and internal wear. Ford released computer updates, but many owners say the problem came back.
issues.next: Have the transmission computer updated and the fluid checked early. If it keeps slipping or drops into limp mode, get a written diagnosis before agreeing to a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: 4-speed automatic slips or fails
issues.sym: The engine revs but the SUV is slow to pick up speed, shifts flare or bang, the overdrive light may blink, and eventually it may not move at all.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic in non-hybrid Escapes of this era wears out early. CarComplaints shows heavy transmission complaint counts for 2002, 2006 and 2008, with failures around 84,000 miles on average.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and color and have codes read as soon as shifting changes. A shop can tell you whether a rebuild, a used unit or a remanufactured transmission makes sense for the car's value.

issues.t: Rear liftgate window shatters on its own
issues.sym: The rear hatch glass suddenly breaks into small pieces, often when the liftgate is closed, sometimes while parked.
issues.why: The cause is not confirmed. Owners suspect stress from the flip-up glass hardware, wiper mount and seal on this window.
issues.next: Cover the opening to keep rain out and avoid driving with loose glass. Call your insurer, since glass coverage often pays for it, and ask a Ford dealer whether any goodwill help is available.

issues.t: Steering wheel may come loose
issues.sym: The steering wheel feels loose, clunks, or shifts on the column.
issues.why: A cracked or badly assembled steering wheel retaining nut could let the wheel loosen. Ford recalled these early vehicles.
issues.next: Do not drive if the wheel feels loose. Check your VIN for the recall.

issues.t: Fuel line O-rings may leak
issues.sym: A gasoline smell under the hood or fuel drips at the front of the vehicle.
issues.why: Damaged O-rings in a fuel line connection could leak fuel near the engine. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Make sure the recall was done. Do not drive with a fuel smell; have it inspected first.

issues.t: Throttle may stick open
issues.sym: The engine does not drop back to idle when you lift off the gas, making the vehicle hard to slow down.
issues.why: On V6 models, the cruise control cable could catch on the engine cover, and on some the accelerator cable could bind, holding the throttle open. Ford issued several recalls.
issues.next: Check for open recalls by VIN. If the throttle sticks, shift to Neutral, brake firmly, and pull over safely.

issues.t: Engine may stall when slowing down
issues.sym: The engine dies as you coast or brake to a stop, leaving you without power steering assist.
issues.why: The engine computer calibration on V6 models could let the idle drop too low during deceleration. Ford reprogrammed the computer under a recall.
issues.next: Have the recall software installed. If the engine stalls, shift to Neutral, restart, and pull over.

issues.t: ABS module fire risk
issues.sym: The ABS light comes on, a burning smell, or smoke near the brake fluid reservoir, even when parked.
issues.why: Brake fluid could leak from the reservoir cap onto the ABS module connector, or the connector seals were missing, letting moisture cause a short and possibly a fire. Ford issued recalls.
issues.next: Make sure both recalls are done. Park outside, away from buildings, until the work is complete.

issues.t: Front lower control arm can rust through
issues.sym: Clunking from the front, wandering steering, or the wheel suddenly shifting position.
issues.why: In states that use road salt, the front lower control arms could corrode and separate, causing a loss of steering control. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done. Any clunk or loose steering should be checked before you drive further.

issues.t: Rear liftgate latch may open in a crash
issues.sym: No warning in normal use; the liftgate could open during a collision if unlocked.
issues.why: The liftgate latch did not meet strength rules. Ford replaced the release rod, clip, and spring under a recall.
issues.next: Check for the recall and keep the liftgate locked while driving.

issues.t: Vehicle may not actually be in Park
issues.sym: The shifter shows Park but the vehicle rolls, or the key comes out while not in Park.
issues.why: A bolt on the shift lever could loosen so the transmission is not in the gear the shifter shows. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the recall is done. Look up your VIN.

issues.t: Hybrid coolant pump failure
issues.sym: Warning lights, reduced power, or the hybrid system shutting down while driving.
issues.why: The electric coolant pump for the hybrid system could fail, causing parts to overheat and the vehicle to lose power. Ford recalled these hybrids.
issues.next: Check for the recall. If the hybrid warning comes on and power drops, pull over safely.

issues.t: Windshield wipers may stop working
issues.sym: Wipers slow down, make noise, or stop in rain or snow.
issues.why: The wiper motor gear could have too little grease, wear out, and fail. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall inspection done before winter driving.

issues.t: Electric power steering assist may cut out
issues.sym: A power steering warning and the steering suddenly becoming very heavy.
issues.why: A torque sensor in the electric power steering could fault and shut off assist. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN. If assist drops out, grip the wheel firmly, slow down, and have it inspected.

issues.t: Park may not hold the vehicle
issues.sym: The vehicle rolls after being put in Park.
issues.why: A retention pin in the park mechanism may be missing. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake and have the recall done.

issues.t: Fuel pump module may crack and leak
issues.sym: A gasoline smell, especially after filling up, or fuel wetness near the rear.
issues.why: The fuel delivery module on top of the tank could crack and leak fuel. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done. Avoid filling the tank to the top until it is fixed.

issues.t: Fuel line can split (do-not-drive recall)
issues.sym: A strong gasoline smell, fuel under the vehicle, or a fire under the hood.
issues.why: A fuel line on the 1.6L engine could split and leak, and a later repair could leave the line misrouted. Ford told owners not to drive until fixed.
issues.next: Confirm all fuel line recalls are done. If you smell fuel, park outside and do not start the engine.

issues.t: 1.6L overheating and cracked head fire risk
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, a low-coolant warning, or smoke and a burning smell from under the hood.
issues.why: The engine could overheat, and running low on coolant could crack the cylinder head and leak oil onto hot parts. Ford issued several recalls.
issues.next: Make sure all recalls are done. Check coolant regularly and stop driving at the first sign of overheating.

issues.t: Shifter cable can come loose
issues.sym: The gear shown on the dash does not match the shifter, or the vehicle moves after you put it in Park.
issues.why: A small bushing that attaches the shift cable to the transmission can wear and fall off. Ford recalled these vehicles more than once.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake until the recall is done. Look up your VIN.

issues.t: Door may not latch
issues.sym: A door looks closed but pops open, or will not stay shut; the door-ajar light may stay on.
issues.why: A part inside the door latch could break, so the door does not latch even though it appears closed. Ford issued two recalls.
issues.next: Have the latches replaced under the recall. Until then, check that each door is fully closed before driving.

issues.t: Coolant leaking into the cylinders
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping with no visible leak, white exhaust smoke at startup, misfires on a cold start, or overheating.
issues.why: Class actions allege that seals in these EcoBoost engines let coolant seep into the cylinders. These are claims, not court findings.
issues.next: Watch the coolant reservoir. If it drops with no outside leak, ask a shop or dealer for a cooling system pressure test before damage spreads.

issues.t: Fuel pump may fail and stall the engine
issues.sym: The engine stalls suddenly and may not restart.
issues.why: The fuel pump could fail without warning. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Check for the recall. If the engine stalls, move out of traffic and call for a tow.

issues.t: Brake hoses may rub and leak
issues.sym: A soft brake pedal, brake warning light, or fluid near a wheel.
issues.why: Incorrect brake hoses could chafe and leak fluid. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done. Do not drive with a soft pedal.

issues.t: Cracked fuel injector fire risk
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell, check engine light, reduced power, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: A fuel injector can crack and leak gasoline onto hot engine parts. Ford issued several recalls, including software that detects the leak and a drain tube, and had to redo some repairs.
issues.next: Have all recalls completed. If you smell raw fuel, park outside and do not drive until it is inspected.

issues.t: Oil separator housing may crack
issues.sym: An oil smell, oil spots under the engine, or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: The oil separator housing can crack and leak oil near hot parts. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done. If you see smoke from under the hood, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Hybrid engine failure can lead to fire
issues.sym: A loud engine noise, sudden loss of power, or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: An internal engine failure can release oil and fuel vapor near hot parts. Ford issued recalls for hybrid and plug-in models, including one for faulty earlier repairs.
issues.next: Check for open recalls. If the engine makes a loud noise and loses power, pull over and shut it off.

issues.t: High-voltage battery cell defect
issues.sym: Hybrid system warnings, reduced power, or the vehicle not starting.
issues.why: A defect in a battery cell can cause an internal short, battery failure, and fire risk. Ford issued recalls.
issues.next: Have the recall done. Follow any parking or charging limits Ford gives until the repair is complete.

issues.t: Transmission may shift into Neutral
issues.sym: The vehicle suddenly loses drive power while moving, as if in Neutral.
issues.why: A software fault in the hybrid powertrain control module can drop the transmission into neutral while you are driving.
issues.next: Have the software update done. If drive is lost, coast to a safe spot and pull over.

issues.t: Rear drive unit may lose oil and seize
issues.sym: A whine or grinding from the rear, then a rear axle locking up.
issues.why: Some all-wheel-drive rear drive units were low on lubricant, which could let the axle seize. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have any rear noise checked right away.

issues.t: Loose transmission bolts may leak fluid
issues.sym: Fluid under the vehicle, a burning smell, or shifting problems.
issues.why: Loose or missing bolts could let transmission fluid leak onto hot parts, risking a fire. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done and do not drive with fluid leaking onto the exhaust.

issues.t: Fuel delivery module may leak and stall
issues.sym: A gasoline smell, rough running, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: The fuel delivery module could leak, causing low fuel pressure and a stall. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Check for the recall. If you smell fuel, park outside and have it inspected.

issues.t: Rear brake linings may be defective
issues.sym: The vehicle takes longer to stop than it should.
issues.why: Some rear brake linings were made incorrectly and may not grip properly. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done soon and leave extra stopping distance until then.

issues.t: Fuel injector O-ring support missing
issues.sym: A gasoline smell under the hood or a check engine light.
issues.why: Some fuel injectors were built without O-ring support discs, so the seal can leak fuel. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done. Do not drive with a strong fuel smell.

issues.t: Adaptive cruise may brake unexpectedly
issues.sym: The vehicle slows or stops on its own with adaptive cruise on, with nothing ahead.
issues.why: A misaligned front radar can make the driver-assist system react to things that are not there. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the radar checked under the recall and be ready to press the gas or turn adaptive cruise off.

issues.t: Cylinder head plugs may leak oil
issues.sym: An oil smell, oil spots under the vehicle, low oil, or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: Ball plugs in the cylinder head could come loose and leak oil onto hot parts, risking a fire. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done. If you see smoke or smell burning oil, pull over and shut off the engine.

issues.t: Brake booster control unit may overheat
issues.sym: Stability or brake warning lights and a harder brake pedal.
issues.why: The electronic brake booster control unit could overheat, cutting brake assist and stability control. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Have the recall done soon. If the pedal turns hard, press firmly and pull over safely.

issues.t: Park may not engage
issues.sym: The vehicle rolls after you select Park.
issues.why: The park function may not engage fully, allowing a rollaway. Ford recalled these vehicles.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake and have the recall done.

issues.t: Throttle body can fail and cut engine power
issues.sym: The wrench or check engine light comes on and the engine drops to a crawl, often while pulling into traffic. It may run normally again after a restart, then do it again.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body's motor and position sensor wear out, so the computer can no longer trust the throttle and puts the engine into a reduced power mode.
issues.next: Have the throttle body tested and replaced. Losing power in traffic is a safety problem, so do not put this off, and ask the dealer whether your vehicle falls under Ford's extended coverage for this part.

issues.t: Shift lever bolt can loosen on a rebuilt transmission (recall 15V-606)
issues.sym: The shifter feels loose or vague, or the gear you select does not match what the vehicle does.
issues.why: On vehicles fitted with a remanufactured automatic, the bolt holding the shift lever to the transmission can work loose so the lever no longer moves the gear selector.
issues.next: Park on level ground, use the parking brake and have the VIN checked for this recall. The vehicle can roll away if it is not really in Park.

issues.t: Engine block heater cord can crack and short out (recall 26V-011)
issues.sym: A tripped outlet or breaker, scorch marks at the cord, or coolant seeping where the heater enters the engine.
issues.why: The block heater element can crack and let coolant reach the electrical connection, which shorts out when the cord is plugged in.
issues.next: Stop using the block heater and have the VIN checked for the recall. A shorted heater can start a fire while the vehicle is parked.

issues.t: Block heater can overheat when plugged in (recall 25V-343)
issues.sym: The block heater cord or the area around it gets very hot, smells of hot plastic, or trips the outlet.
issues.why: The heater can overheat while it is powered, which Ford treats as a fire risk on parked vehicles.
issues.next: Do not plug the block heater in, and have the VIN checked for this recall. The repair is free.

issues.t: Knee airbag may be missing its inflator charge (recall 17V-398)
issues.sym: Nothing is noticeable. The airbag light behaves normally.
issues.why: Some driver knee airbags were built without the material that makes the bag inflate, so it cannot deploy in a crash.
issues.next: Check the VIN with a Ford dealer and have the airbag replaced free of charge.

issues.t: Backup camera image can go blank or distorted (recall 25V-695)
issues.sym: The rear view flickers, shows a scrambled picture, or stays blank when you shift into reverse.
issues.why: A fault in the camera or its wiring interrupts the video signal to the dash screen.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked for the recall and keep checking over your shoulder when reversing until it is fixed.

issues.t: Power windows may not reverse when they hit something (recall 16V-617)
issues.sym: A window keeps closing against a hand or object instead of stopping and dropping back down.
issues.why: The window control settings allow too much closing force before the anti-pinch feature reacts.
issues.next: Have the free software repair done, and keep children away from the switches until it is done.

issues.t: Rear seat belt retractor bolts can be loose (recall 25V-862)
issues.sym: A rear belt may feel loose at its lower mounting, or you can see movement where it bolts to the body.
issues.why: The retractor mounting bolts were not tightened properly, so the belt may not hold an occupant in a crash.
issues.next: Have the VIN checked and the bolts torqued before anyone rides in the back seat.

issues.t: EGR valve can fail and cut engine power (recall 26V-122)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly loses power or stalls, usually with a check engine light.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation valve can fail in a way that upsets the air and fuel mix enough to shut the engine down.
issues.next: Check the VIN for the recall and have the valve replaced. Losing power in traffic is a safety problem, so do not wait.
